messages:
ivy: Running cross-cloud inventory found 3 DB snapshot files: one in s3://redwood-archives/old-snap/db-2019-05.sql.gz and two in gs://redwood-archive/legacy/db-2020-03-part1.dump. None have our internal x-encrypt-meta marker.

omar: Do they show kms metadata from provider-managed SSE? For S3 run `aws s3api head-object --bucket redwood-archives --key old-snap/db-2019-05.sql.gz` and check `ServerSideEncryption`/`SSEKMSKeyId`. For GCS we used `gsutil ls -L`.

ivy: S3 head-object shows `ServerSideEncryption: AES256` (no KMS key). GCS objects show only Content-Type + CRC32C and no kmsKeyName.

chloe: AES256 on S3 is SSE-S3 (provider-managed) which is okay for durability but our compliance needs CMEK or explicit metadata for restores. The mixed-cloud finding complicates restore tooling which expects x-encrypt-meta to know which KMS to call.

sre-oncall: Immediate triage: 1) run CloudTrail/Cloud Logging queries for the insert events to capture uploader SA/role, 2) scan access logs for any GETs from outside our org, 3) quarantine listing in our ticketing system.

omar: CloudTrail query (example): `lookupEvents | filter eventName = "PutObject" and resources[].ARN contains "redwood-archives" and eventTime between 2019 and 2020`

ivy: Logs show uploader on S3 was `legacy-backup@partners.redwood` (partner principal) and GCS uploader was `backup-agent-legacy@redwood-prod.iam.gserviceaccount.com`. No public GETs found.

encops-bot: ALERT: crosscloud_missing_encryption_meta detected: 3 objects. Recommend: small-scale rewrap/rewrite, RBAC hardening, escrow manifest.

chloe: Remediation plan I propose: a) Add an escrow manifest with original object path + upload event id + uploader principal and store it in a restricted CMEK-protected bucket. b) For S3 object, perform `aws s3 cp` -> `aws s3 cp --sse aws:kms --sse-kms-key-id arn:aws:kms:...` to re-encrypt with our KMS; for GCS use `gsutil rewrite -k projects/PROJ/locations/global/keyRings/kr/cryptoKeys/ck`. c) Record all KMS grant IDs and store in the manifest.

omar: Note: S3 re-encrypt via copy will create new put events; make sure to set object ACL/metadata to include x-encrypt-meta so our restore tooling picks it up. Also watch for KMS cross-account grants when partner restores are needed.

sre-oncall: RBAC: remove legacy uploader write privileges immediately and rotate any partner credentials used for uploads. Open infra PR to deny write by default for external principals.

ivy: I'll test a rewrite on one GCS object and one S3 object tonight and post results. Planning to add a nightly scanner to flag objects lacking x-encrypt-meta across clouds.

legal: Tagging legal for visibility. If no external reads it's a compliance remediation; notify customers only if their restores are impacted. Prepare a short template and hold until security confirms impact.

encops-bot: REMINDER: ephemeral KMS grants for partner restores must be TTL-limited and recorded. Use grant TTL 1h and automated revoke script.

chloe: I'll open ENCRYPT-OPS-900, assign to ivy+omar, priority P2, include CloudTrail/Logging queries, sample object list, and commands used. We'll include instructions to populate escrow manifest with the pre-rewrite metadata.

ivy: Test rewrite done: GCS object now shows `kmsKeyName` and S3 object shows `SSEKMSKeyId` after copy. Manifest entry created with original event ids and grant logs. No external reads detected so far.

sre-oncall: Great. Continue bulk rewrite with throttling and KMS request monitoring. If anything shows external access, escalate to #incidents immediately.
